subject: Streaming & concurrency: throughput targets, integration path, and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Foster <naomi.foster@datastream.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:20:00Z
Subject: Streaming & concurrency: throughput targets, integration path, and next steps

Hi Naomi — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap of the call and the concrete next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve included Rachel and Vivek from our team to coordinate the technical run and the deep-dive.

Summary of pain points you described
- Intermittent P95 spikes in production (currently ~800–1200ms for 512-token responses when load peaks)
- Streaming UX: partial token delays and rebuffering create a poor user experience on mobile clients
- High concurrency during business hours (approx 450–600 concurrent active sessions) with bursty peaks that trip your current autoscaler
- Cost sensitivity: you want to avoid a 2–3x token-cost increase while stabilizing latency

Success criteria you mentioned
- P95 latency <= 250ms for 512-token median sessions under steady-state traffic
- Smooth streaming delivery with sub-100ms token intervals (per-chunk) for interactive sessions
- Support 600+ concurrent sessions with predictable tail latency and graceful degradation strategy

Proposed integration path (high-level)
1) Short term: run a perf snapshot with a 2-hour representative traffic replay (we’ll use your trace + synthetic jitter). Goal: identify batching and KV-cache opportunities.
2) Mid term: prototype streaming using Redwood’s chunked streaming API and prefix caching for repeated prompts. Evaluate tokenization delta and per-token timing.
3) Capacity plan: map observed throughput to a Dedicated pool for predictable p95 targets and configure autoscale for bursts; fallback to lower-cost hosted variant for non-critical routes.

Attachments: perf_estimate.xlsx (ballpark resource/costs), infra_topology.png (where we’d place caching / routing).

Next steps (owners & timing)
- Naomi/DataStream: share a representative 2-hour request trace and schema for prompt templates by EOD 2026-12-04 (Naomi) — we need tokenized traces, not just traces of HTTP requests. (Attaching a sample format in the Drive link.)
- Redwood (Rachel): schedule perf replay and produce an initial report within 48 hours of receiving traces.
- Redwood (Vivek): technical deep-dive to review kernel/quantization options and live streaming demo — propose 60-min slot week of 2026-12-07.

If this reads correct, I’ll queue the perf run once we receive the traces and we’ll lock a time for the deep-dive.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Naomi Foster <naomi.foster@datastream.com>

Cc:  
Date: 2026-12-02T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming & concurrency: throughput targets, integration path, and next steps

Jordan — this is perfect, thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications and a bit more color from our side:

Current stack and constraints
- Frontend clients: iOS + Android + thin web client. Mobile clients are most sensitive to token pacing.
- Backend: currently proxying to OpenAI-managed endpoints for generation; we have a Redis layer for short-lived session state but we do not persist KV cache for model tokens.
- Infra: Kubernetes-based API layer, memcached + Redis, EBS-backed storage. GPUs are provisioned through our cloud partner but we do not own Dedicated pools.

Observed behavior
- During a product promo, bursts push concurrent sessions up to ~750 for short intervals — that’s where spikes occur.
- We do see replays where the same prefix is requested often (templated prompts), so prefix/KV caching sounds promising.

Success criteria (confirming)
- Agree with the P95 <= 250ms target as a stretch goal; we’d be happy with a staged plan that gets us to 350ms first if the tradeoff is cost.
- Streaming UX: sub-100ms per-chunk is ideal, but 150ms is acceptable at first.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a sanitized trace file (20261130-p95-traces.log) and a short screenshot of our client metrics to the Drive link you shared. The trace includes token counts and inter-arrival timing.

We’ll aim to share the requested 2-hour request trace by 2026-12-04 EOD. Also happy to do the deep-dive on 2026-12-08 morning PST if that works for your team.

Thanks,

Naomi Foster
Head of Product — ML Integrations
DataStream Inc.
naomi.foster@datastream.com
